content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.15) — model often misses downward momentum, especially after recent dips.
- When sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model overreacts with sharp upward spikes — reduce forecast slope after sentiment reversal.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-forecasting after strong upward moves, under-forecasting after strong downward moves — adjust forecast by 5–10% toward recent 7-day average if sentiment is neutral.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows lagged reaction to sentiment: if sentiment turns positive 3–5 days before forecast, model still underreacts — add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.10.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts > +10% above recent peak, reduce by 5–8% if sentiment remains neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is consistently near zero, model tends to overestimate — apply 3–5% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence bias.
